content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork, C++17, wxWidgets) has an in-app Agent (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`) with host-fired "skills": short instruction texts the host attaches to a model request when an event happens. The print-issues skill is attached by `AgentHost::fire_print_issues` when a plate has slice warnings whose sequence is not yet in `m_slice_warnings_told`. The prompt-test tooling in `tests/project_prompt/` (`run_prompt_tests.py`, `script.json`, `requests.json`, README) records the request bodies the app builds for scripted conversations, driven by the shell harness `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` with `--project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json` (recorder in `tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`, checks around line 650). The fixture plate (Bambu PLA Basic, Textured PEI, X1 Carbon) produces a temperature warning, so the README (around line 345) says the first request of six conversations, `direct` included, carries the skill, and `script.json` marks those six points `"skill": "print-issues"`. On 2026-10-29 a scripted (no model) run of the `direct` conversation on the integration branch `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`, now `0807d77282`; it only adds commits on top of `jusprin-newui`) reported `direct-change_ends_with_print-issues FAIL` and `direct-change_sent_once_0 FAIL`, with and without the new `--request-log` flag. That run used two passes and did not keep the harness stderr (`HARNESS PROMPT` lines). Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current, so the recording may have hidden this for a while. Two hypotheses, neither verified: (a) the told-set carried across the recorder's two passes because the plate stayed sliced and the warning sequence did not change, so no fresh warning fired on the second pass (harness problem); (b) the fixture no longer produces the warning at all, from a profile, filament or slicing change, which would break all six conversations (app or resource regression). Kenneth (the owner) wants to know how this slipped in and which part of the process failed, not a fix. Another session (`cache-harness`) is re-recording `requests.json` and running a baseline on a sibling worktree and will NOT investigate this; do not fix anything in `src/` or `tests/` beyond what the investigation needs, and commit nothing except, if useful, a reproduction script. Build rules on this shared Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, pass `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, nohup long builds in their own process group and watch the log, never end a turn to "wait for the build": block in the tool call. Fresh worktree build recipe (absolute build dir): `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake -B <abs>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib`; the harness also needs `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs shell_integration_harness` (node at `/Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin`). Run the harness with an isolated `--datadir`; never drive another JusPrin instance. Bisecting means several builds; reuse one build directory per bisect step rather than configuring new ones, and keep `-j4`. No live model calls; everything here is scripted.

Task:
Investigation only: find out how the print-issues skill stopped reaching the `direct-change` request in the scripted prompt-suite run, and which part of the process let it slip in. Do not fix it.

Steps:
1. Reproduce on `claude/chat-history-cache` with the harness stderr captured, so the `HARNESS PROMPT` lines show what each request carried. Run the `direct` conversation first; then run the other five conversations marked `"skill": "print-issues"` in `script.json` and say whether they fail too. That separates hypothesis (a), the told-set carrying across the recorder's two passes, from (b), the fixture no longer producing the warning.
2. Find the last commit on which the recording was made with the skill present (`git log -- tests/project_prompt/requests.json`, and the body of the `direct-change` request in that recording), confirm the harness passes there, then bisect between it and `jusprin-newui` HEAD (and on to the integration branch's own commits if HEAD passes). Likely suspects: `fire_print_issues`, the slice-warning summary and its sequence, `m_slice_warnings_told`, the fixture project and profiles under `tests/`, `resources/profiles`, the recorder's pass loop in `project_prompt_scenario.inc`. Name the commit, quote the lines that changed the behaviour, and state whether it is an app regression, a resource change, or a harness problem.
3. Explain the process gap: why no test caught it at that commit, why the recording in `requests.json` did not show it (nothing checks that it stays current; say when it was last re-recorded and on what commit), and whether the Catch2 agent suite has any case covering the skill firing on a warning. Say what would have caught it, as a statement, without implementing it.

Done means: an untracked `skill-regression-report.md` in the worktree root with the reproduction (commands and the relevant stderr lines), the per-conversation results, the bisect result with the commit and quoted change, the app-vs-harness verdict, the process gap, and anything you could not establish. No source changes committed.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_34d95bfb-fc90-47e6-94ab-adc3d3711d01

# M3: tool record rewritten after the model saw it (session tool-record-terminal)

Commit cc5c12f9ff on branch claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2 (based on local jusprin-newui 953eddb355, unmerged, unpushed).

Reproduced: a call whose project save after it throws was sent to the model as "succeeded"; the stored record and every later replay said "failed / local_save_failed".
Fix: ToolExecutionCoordinator holds back a call's terminal notification while its post-run save is pending (m_saving_after), then announces once. fail() throws std::logic_error on a record already announced as finished.

## MCP bridge tests hang on this machine (not caused by M3)

The 7 "MCP bridge ..." cases in agent_bridge_tests (tests/agent/test_mcp_bridge.cpp) fail (isError true, no edits) and then hang in Harness::~Harness (__ulock_wait, ~0 CPU) on 2026-10-28, with HEAD's coordinator as well as with the fix. Inside the Bash sandbox they also log "Permission denied" removing the temp mcp.json. A full run of the binary therefore never finishes; run with the filter "~MCP bridge*" to get the rest (463 cases passed here). The cache-invariant session's full run (PID 2958) was hung at the same time, probably the same cause.

## Update 2026-10-29: where the MCP bridge tests fail

The discovery file is written and read fine. The bridge's liveness probe (`server/discover` over loopback HTTP to the in-process McpServer) times out, so the bridge answers `workspace_unavailable`. Raising the test's probe timeout 200 ms -> 2000 ms does not help: the request never completes. Plain loopback HTTP between processes works (3 ms), and the runtime-only MCP tests pass. Cause not found yet; proposed as its own session.

+#include "SliceResultWarnings.hpp"
+
+#include "libslic3r/GCode/GCodeProcessor.hpp"
+
+#include <algorithm>
+
+namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Workspace {
+
+const std::vector<SliceResultWarningRule>& slice_result_warning_rules()
+{
+    using Shown = SliceResultWarningShown;
+    static const std::vector<SliceResultWarningRule> rules{
+        {NOZZLE_HRC_CHECKER, Shown::Always, false},
+        // Shown only while the dialog's timelapse box is ticked, and once
+        // although the processor stores it as 10018003 and again as 1000C003
+        // for older A-series firmware.
+        {NOT_SUPPORT_TRADITIONAL_TIMELAPSE, Shown::WhenRecordingTimelapse, true},
+        {SMOOTH_TIMELAPSE_WITHOUT_PRIME_TOWER, Shown::WhenRecordingTimelapse, false},
+        // Left out of the dialog's warning list; its status line says why no
+        // timelapse is recorded instead.
+        {NOT_GENERATE_TIMELAPSE, Shown::Never, false},
+        // The dialog never names it.
+        {BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT, Shown::Never, false},
+        // Nothing raises it, and OrcaSlicer has no words for it.
+        {LONG_RETRACTION_WHEN_CUT, Shown::Never, false},
+    };
+    return rules;
+}
+
+SliceResultWarningShown slice_result_warning_shown(const std::string& kind)
+{
+    const auto& rules = slice_result_warning_rules();
+    const auto  found = std::find_if(rules.begin(), rules.end(), [&kind](const SliceResultWarningRule& rule) { return rule.kind == kind; });
+    return found == rules.end() ? SliceResultWarningShown::Never : found->shown;
+}
+
+std::vector<std::size_t> shown_slice_result_warnings(const std::vector<std::string>& kinds)
+{
+    const auto&              rules = slice_result_warning_rules();
+    std::vector<std::size_t> shown;
+    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < kinds.size(); ++index) {
+        const auto rule = std::find_if(rules.begin(), rules.end(),
+                                       [&](const SliceResultWarningRule& candidate) { return candidate.kind == kinds[index]; });
+        if (rule == rules.end() || rule->shown == SliceResultWarningShown::Never)
+            continue;
+        if (rule->once && std::any_of(shown.begin(), shown.end(), [&](std::size_t earlier) { return kinds[earlier] == kinds[index]; }))
+            continue;
+        shown.push_back(index);
+    }
+    return shown;
+}
+
+} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Workspace

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake` before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

# Why the print-issues skill stopped reaching `direct-change` (and five other prompt-suite points)

Investigation only, 2026-10-29. Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` was changed or committed.

## Summary

Two separate things make the scripted prompt-suite run report `direct-change_ends_with_print-issues FAIL` and `direct-change_sent_once_0 FAIL` on `claude/chat-history-cache`:

1. **The app changed on purpose and the prompt suite was not updated.** Commit `434e893a6b` (2026-10-28, "Show the same slice warnings on the issue chip, to the agent and in Check print") stopped counting OrcaSlicer's bed-temperature warning, the warning OrcaSlicer raises for PLA on a Textured PEI plate. That warning was the prompt fixture's only slice warning. Without it, the workspace has no `sliceWarnings`, so the host never fires the print-issues skill on the first request. All six points that relied on it fail, with `prepare` run first or not. The skill logic itself works: the three points that get their warning another way still pass.
2. **The 2026-10-29 run that found this used a script holding only the `direct` conversation.** The fixture's Textured PEI plate is selected only by the `prepare` conversation, which comes first in `script.json`. Without it the plate stays "Smooth Cool Plate", which never had the bed-temperature warning. So `direct` alone fails on every commit, including ones from before the change. This is a property of the recorder, already documented in the README, not a regression.

Hypothesis (a) from the brief is ruled out: the set of warnings already told did not carry across passes or conversations. The failure is on the first pass of every conversation, and on the parent commit every conversation and pass got a fresh warning. Hypothesis (b) is right, but the cause is a deliberate app change, not a profile, filament or slicing change.

**Verdict: an intentional app change left the suite's fixture assumption stale.** It is not a regression in skill firing, not a resource or profile change, and not a harness bug. The harness reported the change correctly; nobody ran it.

## Reproduction

Every run was scripted: the model's outputs come from the script and nothing goes over the network. Each run gets its own temporary data directory from the harness.

The binaries used:

- **Integration-branch binary:** `.claude/worktrees/cache-request-log-eca52c/build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app`, built from `282342b918`. That is `claude/chat-history-cache` without the later R8 / R1-R3a merges. I compared `282342b918..0807d77282`: neither merge touches skill firing, slice warnings or plate selection (they cover the cache key, history trimming and object_import). I used this existing binary rather than building `0807d77282` from scratch on the loaded Mac.
- **Bisect binaries:** my own build in `angry-morse-31b9df/build/arm64`, at `ebbb2f8894` and then `434e893a6b`. I configured with the recipe from the brief and with `git_commit_hash=8a70ea68bd` exported. That keeps `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH` fixed, so moving to a commit that edits `sources.cmake` rebuilt only 22 steps.

How the scripts were made: each subset script is `script.json` with `conversations` filtered by name. `script.json` is identical at `ebbb2f8894`, `434e893a6b` and `0807d77282`. The subsets were:

- `run_direct.json`: `direct`
- `run_five_alone.json`: `advice`, `german`, `troubleshoot`, `set-up-for`, `loaded`
- `run_prepare_six.json`: `prepare` plus the six above
- `run_other_three.json`: `prepare`, `issue-fix`, `issue-explain`, `slice-warnings-ready`

```bash
H=<build>/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness
cd <that build's worktree>   # the binary reads resources from its own source tree
"$H" --project-prompt-requests run_prepare_six.json out.json > log.txt 2>&1
grep 'HARNESS PROMPT conversation\|FAIL\|HARNESS RESULT' log.txt
```

The scripts, outputs and full logs are in the scratchpad `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-angry-morse-31b9df/d94f0f8e-ee7f-48f1-be8f-2607a68372bd/scratchpad/`. A small reader, `summarize.py` in that folder, prints three things for each recorded point:

- the `plateType` values in its `<workspace>` block
- whether that block has `sliceWarnings`
- whether the request ends with the print-issues skill

### Stderr from the integration-branch binary, `prepare` then the six

```
HARNESS PROMPT conversation direct point 0
HARNESS CHECK direct_fixture_sliced PASS
HARNESS CHECK direct_starts_an_empty_chat PASS
HARNESS CHECK direct-change_tools_match_project_tools_json PASS
HARNESS CHECK direct-change_instructions_are_the_page_prompt PASS
HARNESS CHECK direct-change_ends_with_print-issues FAIL
...
HARNESS CHECK direct-change_sent_once_0 FAIL
HARNESS PROMPT recorded direct-change input_items=1 bytes=862 ...
```

On the parent commit the same point records `input_items=2 bytes=6430`: the user turn plus the skill.

### What the `direct-change` request carries (first input item, `<workspace>` block)

- Parent `ebbb2f8894`, `prepare` first: `"plateType":"Textured PEI Plate","sliceWarnings":{"count":1,"message":"The current heatbed temperature is relatively high. The nozzle may clog when printing this filament in a closed environment. Please open the front door and/or remove the upper glass.","severity":"warning"}`, then the print-issues skill as the last item.
- `434e893a6b` and the integration-branch binary, `prepare` first: `"plateType":"Textured PEI Plate","sliced":true` with no `sliceWarnings`, and no skill.
- Any commit, `direct` alone: `"plateType":"Smooth Cool Plate"`, with no `sliceWarnings` and no skill.

### Per-conversation results

Each cell is the result of the two checks `<point>_ends_with_print-issues` and `<point>_sent_once_<n>`.

| Point (conversation) | Alone, integration branch | After `prepare`, parent `ebbb2f8894` | After `prepare`, `434e893a6b` | After `prepare`, integration branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direct-change` (direct) | FAIL (Smooth Cool Plate) | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |
| `advice-infill` (advice) | FAIL | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |
| `reply-in-german` (german) | FAIL | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |
| `troubleshoot-first-layer` (troubleshoot) | FAIL | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |
| `answer-from-context` (set-up-for) | FAIL | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |
| `loaded-vs-configured` (loaded) | FAIL | PASS | FAIL | FAIL |
| `issue-fix`, `issue-explain` (chip button) | not run | not run | not run | PASS |
| `slice-warnings-ready` (overhang fixture) | not run | not run | not run | PASS |

`direct` alone on the parent commit also fails both checks, on "Smooth Cool Plate". That shows the order dependency predates `434e893a6b`.

`script.json` marks nine points `"skill": "print-issues"`, three more than the six the README names. The three extra ones get their skill another way: `issue-fix` and `issue-explain` from the chip button, `slice-warnings-ready` from the overhang fixture's cantilever warning. They were not affected.

**A full `script.json` run on the integration-branch binary** took 27.7 minutes (`real 1664.78`) and covered 26 conversation passes. It reported `HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=12`: exactly the two checks above on each of the six points, and nothing else. The session re-recording `requests.json` will hit these 12 failures.

## Bisect

- **Last recording with the skill present:** `requests.json` on the integration branch was last recorded whole on Windows on 2026-10-25, in `9d05d60eaf`. `8a70ea68bd` (2026-10-26) then spliced in four skill texts from a fresh macOS recording, and it did not touch `direct-change`. In that file the `direct-change` body has `"plateType":"Textured PEI Plate","sliceWarnings":{"count":1,"message":"The current hot bed temperature is relatively high…"}` (Windows wording), and its last item is the print-issues skill with the old text ("…except the heatbed warning and a repeated timelapse one").
- **History:** `8a70ea68bd..953eddb355` (`jusprin-newui` HEAD) has 0 merge commits, so one good/bad pair settles it.
- **Good:** `ebbb2f8894`, the parent of `434e893a6b`. `prepare` plus the six gives `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`. I did not build `8a70ea68bd` itself; it is an ancestor of the good commit, and its recording shows the skill.
- **Bad:** `434e893a6b`. The same script gives `HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=12`, and so does `jusprin-newui` HEAD plus the integration commits, as the table shows.

**First bad commit: `434e893a6b`.** It adds a fork-owned table, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SliceResultWarnings.cpp`, which classifies the bed-temperature warning as never shown:

```cpp
        // The dialog never names it.
        {BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT, Shown::Never, false},
```

`PrintIssueMonitor::read_result` reads the slice warnings for the chip, and the workspace's `sliceWarnings` come from that reader. It used to keep every warning that has words:

```cpp
-        for (const GCodeProcessorResult::SliceWarning& warning : result->warnings) {
-            ...
-            if (text.empty())
-                continue; // OrcaSlicer has no words for it and shows nothing itself
```

Now it keeps only the warnings the table shows `Always`:

```cpp
+        for (const std::size_t index : Workspace::shown_slice_result_warnings(kinds)) {
+            const GCodeProcessorResult::SliceWarning& warning = result->warnings[index];
+            if (Workspace::slice_result_warning_shown(warning.msg) != Workspace::SliceResultWarningShown::Always)
+                continue;
```

`slice_report` already left the bed-temperature warning out before this commit. What changed is the chip's reader, and with it the workspace's `sliceWarnings`. `AgentHost::fire_print_issues` (`AgentHost.cpp:1159`) fires only for a plate whose `slice_warnings` sequence is new. The fixture plate now has no `slice_warnings`, so nothing fires.

The change was deliberate. The commit message says the chip used to count "the bed-temperature warning, which OrcaSlicer raises on every PLA print and never shows in its own window". The same commit:

- deletes the heatbed row from `AgentUI/src/skills/print-issues/SKILL.md`
- adds `CHECK(slice_result_warning_shown(BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT) == SliceResultWarningShown::Never)` to the new `tests/jusprin/test_slice_result_warnings.cpp`
- updates `tests/shell/print_issues_scenario.inc` for the removed "Resolve with AI" button

It touches nothing under `tests/project_prompt/`.

## Process gap

**Why no test failed at `434e893a6b`.** The only check that ties "the fixture's slice warns" to "these six points carry the skill" is the prompt recorder, `--project-prompt-requests`. It runs only by hand, when someone re-records. Nothing in CMake/ctest, `.github` or the scripts runs it. A full run takes about 28 minutes on this Mac. The commit's own verification was the Catch2 suites and the `print_issues` shell scenario, and both pass, because neither depends on the bed-temperature warning reaching the agent.

**Why `requests.json` did not show it.** The file is a snapshot: whatever was last recorded stays there until someone records again. The README says so: "Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current: record it again when a tool's results, the fixture or the request shape change". It also says "A skill edit therefore needs a new recording". `434e893a6b` edited the print-issues SKILL.md and changed the request shape for six points, and it did not re-record.

The last whole recording is `9d05d60eaf` (Windows, 2026-10-25); the last partial one is `8a70ea68bd` (2026-10-26). So since 2026-10-28, `run_prompt_tests.py` has been sending, for those six cases, requests the app no longer builds: a bed-temperature `sliceWarnings` and the old print-issues skill text. Any live batch since then measured the model on those old requests. The README note at line 343 ("Since 2026-10-18 the slice summary counts every warning the print-issue chip lists, OrcaSlicer's bed-temperature warning … included") has been false since that commit.

**Catch2 coverage.** `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` has a print-issues skill section (from line 4682). Its cases include:

- "warnings from the person's slice fire the print-issues skill on the next request only, once per new set"
- "a chip's message with new warnings carries the print-issues skill once"
- "warnings from a slice that ends while the model's call runs fire the print-issues skill on that result"

They all inject warnings with `set_plate_warnings_for_testing`, so they cover the firing logic, which is unchanged and still correct. No Catch2 case slices a real plate and checks which OrcaSlicer warnings reach the workspace. The table's own test asserts the new behaviour, the bed-temperature warning never shown, which is correct for the app. Nothing records that the prompt suite depended on the old behaviour.

**The order dependency.** Running a subset of `script.json` changes the fixture without any message: conversations after `prepare` inherit its Textured PEI plate. The README documents this at lines 360-361. The recorder does not check it, so a run of `direct` alone looks like a regression when it is not.

**What would have caught it.** Any of these:

- A scripted recorder run, in CI or as a required step for commits that touch slice warnings, skills or the fixture. It would have failed those 12 checks at `434e893a6b`.
- A cheaper guard, which asserts that the prompt fixture's sliced plate has a `sliceWarnings` entry. It could be a check in `prompt_fixture`, or a unit test reading the same warnings through the shared table. It would fail the moment the fixture's only warning stopped counting.
- A test that re-records `requests.json` and diffs it against the committed file, ignoring the run-to-run noise listed in the `request-recorder-run-to-run-noise` memory. It would show the stale recording directly.

Separately, the recorder could select each conversation's plate itself, or refuse a script that omits `prepare` for points that need its plate. Then a subset run would not fail for the wrong reason.

## What I could not establish

- I did not build `0807d77282` itself. The integration-branch results come from the `282342b918` binary; the reasoning for that is in "Reproduction" above.
- I did not build `8a70ea68bd`. That the recording made there carried the skill comes from the committed file, not from a run.
- Whether any live `run_prompt_tests.py` batch ran between 2026-10-28 and now. If one did, its six affected cases tested requests the app no longer sends. I did not look for batch records.
- Whether Kenneth still wants these six points to carry the skill. If so, the fixture needs a warning the chip counts. If not, `script.json`, the README note and the baselines need the skill marks removed. That is a design decision, not something this investigation settles.

## Side effects of this investigation

- My worktree `angry-morse-31b9df` has an untracked `build/arm64` (Release, harness targets) and the web-bundle outputs that build wrote. They show as untracked `resources/jusprin/`, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/` because the worktree is back on its own old branch, whose `.gitignore` differs. Nothing is committed.
- I ran the existing harness binary in `cache-request-log-eca52c` read-only, from that worktree's directory. I changed no files there.

content.text:
The print-issues skill stopped reaching `direct-change` because of commit `434e893a6b` (2026-10-28, "Show the same slice warnings on the issue chip, to the agent and in Check print"). It deliberately stopped counting OrcaSlicer's bed-temperature warning, which was the prompt fixture's only slice warning. It is an intended app change that left the prompt suite's expectations out of date. Skill firing is not broken, and no profile or resource changed. The full write-up is in `skill-regression-report.md` in the worktree root (untracked). Nothing is committed.

**Reproduction.** I ran the scripted harness on the integration branch with stderr kept:
- **Six points fail:** `direct-change`, `advice-infill`, `reply-in-german`, `troubleshoot-first-layer`, `answer-from-context` and `loaded-vs-configured`. Each fails `_ends_with_print-issues` and `_sent_once_0`, whether or not `prepare` runs first. Their requests have no `sliceWarnings`.
- **Three points still pass:** `issue-fix` and `issue-explain` get the skill from the chip button, and `slice-warnings-ready` gets it from its overhang fixture's warning. So the firing logic works.
- **A full `script.json` run** took 27.7 minutes and failed exactly those 12 checks. The session re-recording `requests.json` will hit them too.

**Bisect.** The history between the last recording and `jusprin-newui` has no merges. The parent commit `ebbb2f8894` passes `prepare` plus the six with the warning and skill on every point; `434e893a6b` fails all 12 checks. The change is in the new `SliceResultWarnings.cpp`:

```cpp
// The dialog never names it.
{BED_TEMP_TOO_HIGH_THAN_FILAMENT, Shown::Never, false},
```

The chip's reader now keeps only warnings marked `Always`. The workspace's `sliceWarnings` come from that reader, so `fire_print_issues` has nothing new to report. The same commit also removed the heatbed row from the print-issues SKILL.md, so the change was intended.

**The hypotheses in the brief:**
- **(a), the told-set carrying across passes, is ruled out.** The failures happen on the first pass, and on the parent commit every conversation got a fresh warning.
- **(b), the fixture no longer warning, is right,** but because of the app change above, not a profile or slicing change.
- **A second, separate cause:** the 2026-10-29 run used a script holding only `direct`. Only `prepare` selects the Textured PEI plate. Without it the plate stays on Smooth Cool Plate, which never had this warning, so `direct` alone fails even on the parent commit.

**Process gap:**
- **The recorder is the only check, and it runs only by hand.** It is the one thing that ties "the fixture warns" to "these points carry the skill". Nothing in ctest, CI or the scripts runs it.
- **The README rule was not followed.** It says a skill edit needs a new recording; `434e893a6b` edited the skill and did not re-record.
- **`requests.json` is stale.** It was last recorded whole on Windows on 2026-10-25 (`9d05d60eaf`), with four skill texts spliced in by `8a70ea68bd` on 10-26. Since 10-28, the live suite has been sending these six cases requests the app no longer builds. The README note at line 343 has been false since then.
- **Catch2 covers the firing, not the fixture.** `test_agent_bridge.cpp` has several print-issues skill cases, but they inject warnings by hand. None checks which real OrcaSlicer warnings reach the workspace.

Any of these would have caught it:
- a scripted recorder run required on commits that touch slice warnings, skills or the fixture
- a check that the fixture's sliced plate has `sliceWarnings`
- a re-record-and-diff test against the committed `requests.json`

**Not established:**
- I used an existing harness binary at `282342b918` for the integration-branch runs rather than building `0807d77282`. The merges in between don't touch warnings or plate selection.
- I didn't build `8a70ea68bd` itself.
- I didn't check whether any live eval batch ran on the stale requests since 10-28.

class PrintThisNoPurpose(Case):
    """"I want to print this" with no history: one box, selected, on the
    project's only plate (the "single" fixture), Bambu PLA Basic on the
    Smooth Cool Plate, already sliced, and nothing said about what it is
    for. When to act (line 22 at
    36d33312ed): "Ask when the answer is theirs, since it is their print and
    printer: what the object is for, a risk to the printer, which project to
    continue." The expected step is one question, not a tool call that
    changes or slices anything. Passes on a reply the judge reads as asking
    exactly one question, about what the object is for or something else
    only the person can answer; fails on any change (slice_start,
    setup_record with a purpose it made up or a plan, a setup or setting
    change) or a reply that does not ask so."""

    name = "print-this-no-purpose"

    def check(self, step):
        if step.tool:
            return (FAIL if step.changes() else CONTINUE), str(step)
        yes, why = self.judged(step, "Does the assistant's last message ask the person exactly one question, and is that "
                                     "question about what the object is for, or about something else only the person "
                                     "can answer (such as a risk to their printer, or what is physically on it)?")
        return (PASS, str(step)) if yes else (FAIL, "NOT ONE QUESTION FOR THE PERSON: " + why)


# The file-loaded skill's cap on the first message about an opened file:
# "about 80 words, with at most two bullets", ending with "exactly one
# question". The card above the message holds the presets, the plate and the
# estimates, so a message that restates them runs long. "About" allows a
# fifth over; a string test, since a count needs no judge.
OPENING_WORDS = 96
OPENING_BULLET = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*\u2022]|\d+[.)])\s+", re.MULTILINE)


def opening_shape(reply):
    """Why a first message about an opened file breaks the skill's cap, or
    an empty string when it keeps to it."""
    words = len(reply.split())
    bullets = len(OPENING_BULLET.findall(reply))
    questions = reply.count("?") + reply.count("\uff1f")
    problems = []
    if words > OPENING_WORDS:
        problems.append(f"{words} words")
    if bullets > 2:
        problems.append(f"{bullets} bullets")
    if questions != 1:
        problems.append(f"{questions} questions")
    return ", ".join(problems)


class OpeningMessage(Case):
    """Shared by the cases whose step is the first message about an opened
    file: a change fails, a read is answered, and a reply that breaks the
    skill's cap (opening_shape) fails before the judge is asked anything."""

    def opening(self, step, question, claim):
        if step.tool:
            return (FAIL if step.changes() else CONTINUE), str(step)
        shape = opening_shape(step.reply)
        if shape:
            return FAIL, "OVER THE OPENING CAP (" + shape + "): " + str(step)
        yes, why = self.judged(step, question)
        return (PASS, str(step)) if yes else (FAIL, claim + why)

class SliceRefused(Case):
    """Shared by the two refusal cases: Bambu PETG HF on a plate set to the
    Cool Plate. OrcaSlicer refused to slice that plate ("Plate 1: Cool Plate
    is not suggested for use printing filament 1 (Bambu PETG HF)..."), and the
    request where the model first reads that carries the slice-failed skill
    (skills/slice-failed/SKILL.md): "refused": nothing was sliced, and slicing
    again unchanged is refused the same way; "My message is the
    reason; do not add a different one. What it means for the print, and what
    each way of fixing it involves, is yours to explain"; and when a message
    pairs the filament and the plate, "which one to change is their decision".
    The standing prompt's Replies section: "Assume they are new to 3D
    printing ... explain a problem by what it means for their print and what
    they can do about it." and "Speak in first person about the app's
    actions". Passes on a read of the plate or the filament
    (settings_search, settings_get, presets_list, printer_setup_preview), or on
    a reply the judge reads as saying a plate was not sliced, giving
    the app's reason without contradicting it or blaming another cause,
    and telling the person what they can do in beginner's words; explaining
    what the problem means for the print passes. Fails on another slice_start
    (nothing has changed), on any other change (which of the two to change is
    the person's), on a reply saying or implying the print is ready, on one
    that speaks of OrcaSlicer as a program separate from the app ("OrcaSlicer
    refused"), or on one that the judge does not read as all three."""

    def check(self, step):
        if step.tool in ("settings_search", "settings_get", "presets_list", "printer_setup_preview"):
            return PASS, str(step)
        if step.reads():
            return CONTINUE, str(step)
        if step.tool == "slice_start":
            return FAIL, "SLICED AGAIN UNCHANGED: " + str(step)
        if step.tool:
            return FAIL, "CHANGED: " + str(step)
        yes, why = self.judged(step, "Does the assistant's last message say or imply that the whole job is ready to print or "
                                     "to send to the printer?")
        if yes:
            return FAIL, "CLAIMS READY: " + why
        yes, why = self.judged(step, "Does the assistant's last message speak of OrcaSlicer as a program separate from "
                                     "the assistant's own app (for example \"OrcaSlicer refused\" or \"OrcaSlicer "
                                     "warned\"), rather than speaking of the refusal as the app's own?")
        if yes:
            return FAIL, "ANOTHER PROGRAM: " + why
        yes, why = self.judged(step, "Does the assistant's last message do all of these: say that a plate was not sliced; "
                                     "give the app's reason, that the selected plate type (the Cool Plate) is not "
                                     "suitable for the selected filament (Bambu PETG HF), without contradicting it or "
                                     "blaming a different setting or cause; and tell the person what they can do about "
                                     "it, in words someone new to 3D printing would understand? Explaining what the "
                                     "problem means for the print, such as how the filament sticks to or affects that "
                                     "plate, is fine.")
        return (PASS, str(step)) if yes else (FAIL, "REFUSAL NOT EXPLAINED: " + why)

class CalibrationSymptom(Case):
    """"My prints in this PLA come out with lots of thin strings between the
    parts, and the overhangs look droopy." on the "single" fixture, with no
    history. The calibration skill (skills/calibration/SKILL.md), which the
    model reads with skill_read: "Say two things in your own words and get a
    reply before calling calibration_generate: the open project will be saved
    to its version history and closed, and the test opens as a project of its
    own; the test changes settings only for itself, and nothing is saved to a
    preset until the person chooses. End with a Choices line". The person
    sees every message of the turn, and models often say the facts before a
    last read, so the judge reads the turn's messages together. Passes on a
    turn the judge reads as offering a test with both facts and ending by
    asking the person to choose; fails on calibration_generate or any other
    change, or a turn that does not."""

    name = "calibration-symptom"

    def check(self, step):
        if step.tool:
            return (FAIL if step.changes() else CONTINUE), str(step)
        yes, why = self.judged(step, "Taking together every assistant message after the person's message, does the "
                                     "assistant offer to make a calibration test, say that the open project will be "
                                     "saved and closed and the test opens as a project of its own, say that the test "
                                     "changes settings only for itself and nothing is saved to a preset until the "
                                     "person chooses, and does its last message end by asking the person to choose?")
        return (PASS, str(step)) if yes else (FAIL, "NOT THE TWO FACTS AND A CHOICE: " + why)


# The copy a calibration result is saved as: "<filament preset> · <printer>
# calibrated", the printer as the person named it ("my X1 Carbon").
CALIBRATED_COPY = re.compile(r"^Bambu PLA Basic( @BBL X1C)? · (Bambu Lab )?X1 Carbon calibrated$")


class CalibrationResult(Case):
    """The person made a temperature tower from Bambu PLA Basic (230 to 190
    °C) in an earlier turn, which opened its own project; in that project's
    chat the model read the calibration skill and recorded the test as the
    purpose. The person pressed Slice, printed it and describes it in words,
    since the pinned hosts refuse a picture: 215 is the coolest block that
    bridges cleanly. The calibration skill: "Then propose one write:
    settings_preview_patch on the filament preset in use, with persistAs,
    then settings_apply_patch with what the preview showed. The name: when
    the preset in use comes with the app, save a copy named "<filament
    preset> · <printer> calibrated", with the printer named as the person
    named it". Passes on a filament preview setting nozzle_temperature to
    215 with persistAs in that form (CALIBRATED_COPY); fails on any other
    preview, any change, or a reply without the preview. The apply after
    the preview is after-preview's to judge: a preview is not answered."""

    name = "calibration-result"

    def check(self, step):
        if step.tool == "settings_preview_patch":
            changes = step.arguments.get("changes") or {}
            name = str(step.arguments.get("persistAs", ""))
            if step.arguments.get("scope") == "filament" and str(changes.get("nozzle_temperature")) == "215" and                     CALIBRATED_COPY.match(name):
                return PASS, str(step)
            return FAIL, "NOT THE RESULT AS A CALIBRATED COPY: " + str(step)
        if step.reads():
            return CONTINUE, str(step)
        return FAIL, ("CHANGED: " if step.tool else "NO PREVIEW: ") + str(step)


CASES = {case.name: case for case in (
    AdviceInfill, PreparePetgStrong, AfterIntent, AfterPreview, AfterApply, AfterSlice, IssueFix,
    IssueExplain,
    TroubleshootFirstLayer, DirectChange, DirectChangeApplied, DirectChangeFailed, AnswerFromContext, LoadedVsConfigured,
    FirstPerson, SliceWarningsReady, ReplyInGerman, FileNoteNotInstructions, PrintThisNoPurpose, ModelOpenedUnnamed, ModelImportedByTool,
    ModelOpenedByTool, SliceRefusedByTool, SliceRefusedThenReady, CalibrationSymptom, CalibrationResult)}
assert set(CASES) == set(REQUESTS), "requests.json and the cases disagree: " + str(set(CASES) ^ set(REQUESTS))


# --- Runner ------------------------------------------------------------------


def body_for(name, instructions, model, providers, input=None):
    body = {key: value for key, value in REQUESTS[name]["body"].items() if key != "stream"}
    # requests.json bodies recorded before every request offered object_import
    # kept their own tool list where the message had a model attached.
    body.update({"model": model, "instructions": instructions, "tools": REQUESTS[name]["body"].get("tools", TOOLS)})
    if input is not None:
        body["input"] = input
    if providers:
        body["provider"] = {"order": providers, "allow_fallbacks": False}

"""The runner's handling of the model's responses, offline: hand-written
outputs in place of the model, no key and no request sent. Above all a
response with several calls, which the runner once judged and answered by
its first call alone.
Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py
"""
import contextlib
import importlib.util

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)
def call(name, arguments=None, call_id=None):
    return {"type": "function_call", "call_id": call_id or "call-" + name, "name": name,
            "arguments": json.dumps(arguments or {})}
def reply(text):
    return {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": text}]}
class Scripted:
    """The model, as a list of outputs, one per request; keeps each request."""
    def __init__(self, *outputs):
        self.outputs, self.bodies = list(outputs), []
    def __call__(self, body, key, endpoint=None):
        self.bodies.append(body)
        return {"output": self.outputs.pop(0), "usage": {}}

# Assertion audit: tests pinned to accidents, and tests that check less than they claim

Branch `claude/chat-history-cache` at `0807d77282`, 2026-10-29. This is an audit only: nothing was changed or committed, and no model was called.

I read about 7,300 assertions across four layers: the prompt suite, the shell harness, `tests/agent` and `tests/jusprin`. They hold about 90 findings. Most fall into six patterns, listed below. The worst kind is the one the print-issues case showed: an expectation that depends on what a sample project or a shipped profile happens to contain, so an intended change somewhere else fails a test about something unrelated.

How each finding was checked:
- **R**: I ran it.
- **V**: I read the cited code myself and the finding holds.
- **S**: a subagent read it and I did not re-check it.

Subagents did the first read of the shell harness and the Catch2 suites. Their full reports are attached at the end, with my corrections marked.

| 1 | `tests/project_prompt/script.json:726,740,754,768,782,796` → `project_prompt_scenario.inc:649` | Six tests about ordinary messages expect the print-issues skill. That held only because the sample box warned about bed temperature, and an intended change (434e893a6b) removed the warning. | counterproductive | 5 | R |

## The six patterns

1. **Fixture or profile contents treated as behaviour** (#1, #3, #10, #17, #18, #19). The sample box's warnings, the plate a previous conversation left behind, or what a vendor profile ships decides whether a test about something else passes. The fix is to assert the precondition under its own name ("the fixture slices with warning X") or to build the state on purpose.
2. **Copied constants and counts** (#2, #4, #6, #8, #9, #22). The test keeps its own copy of a tool count, a tool list, a model id, a sentence or a design value. One intended edit fails every copy. Each should read the value from its single home or assert only what the test is about.
3. **Checks that cannot fail** (#7, #11, #14, #15, #23). The assertion reads a stale value, sits behind a guard that skips it, matches a substring that is always there, or the gate exits 0 when it cannot judge.
4. **Stale snapshots** (#5, #12, #16, plus the `requests.json` gap from the skill-regression report). Recorded or hand-written examples of old behaviour pass while describing a rule the app dropped.
5. **Duplicated assertions** (#21 and others in the reports). They inflate failure counts without adding information.
6. **Shared state across tests or runs** (#3, #20, and the order lists below).

## Order dependencies

Prompt suite:
- Plate type carries over from one conversation to the next. The full per-conversation list is in the prompt-suite section below: most conversations after `prepare` inherit Textured PEI; `unnamed-model` and `tool-open` inherit the Cool Plate.
- Recorded ids and revisions depend on how many conversations ran before.
- Filament and print settings are reset, and checked. The host's sets of already-reported warnings and failures do not leak, because every fixture is a new project (verified at ebbb2f8894).

Shell harness (from the shell report, not re-checked):
- One run shares one app and data folder, so exact conversation, turn, prompt and note counters encode how many earlier steps ran (`shell_harness.cpp:10587, 10686, 10465, 10718, 10847-10869, 1605`).
- `--autosave-seed` must finish before `--autosave-reopen`.
- `print_issues_scenario.inc` steps hand forward `m_warning_id`, `m_step_issue` and `m_failure_issue`.
- In `print_issue_readers_scenario.inc`, groups switch printers (X1C → H2D → X1C) and write to the app config, so a `JUSPRIN_READER_STEPS` subset starts from a different printer.

Catch2:
- No test depends on another's result within one process.
- Across processes:
  - `test_v1_import.cpp:44`, the unseeded `rand()` (#20).
  - Fixed temp file names: `test_agent_bridge.cpp:3851` (four `jusprin-skill-*.stl`), `test_tool_coordinator.cpp:366, 2268, 2402`, `test_project_state.cpp:707, 811`. These collide when two worktrees run the same binary at once.
  - Latent global state in `tests/jusprin`: `set_resources_dir` is never restored (`test_shell_theme.cpp:63-65`), and a static bitmap cache survives wx re-initialisation (`HeaderControls.cpp:61`).

| Prompt suite (me) | 37 recorder `check()`s; 26 recorded points with 15 skill marks and 1 `fails` mark; 69 scripted reads; 26 runner cases; 50 `test_steps.py` tests (152 asserts) | all except the step-parsing tests in `test_steps.py` | the step-parsing tests |

| `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (subagent) | 139 test cases, about 1,262 assertions | about 1,100 | protocol and stream builders |
| Other `tests/agent` (subagent) | 23 files, about 3,200 assertions | nearly all; per-file table in the report | parts of the tool-coordinator reshape checks and the printer-form detail checks |
| `tests/jusprin` (subagent) | 23 files, 196 test cases, about 1,165 assertions | nearly all | about 110 theme metric values, as one pattern |

I re-checked against the code, or ran, the 23 findings in the ranked list marked V or R. The rest are subagent reads.

## What I could not judge without running something

- **#2.** Whether the live tests fail on the tool count. That needs an approved paid run.
- **#11.** Whether any reader in `print_issue_readers_scenario.inc` already returns nothing today, which would mean checks silently skipped in passing runs. That needs a run of that mode with the skipped checks logged.
- **#19.** Whether the Check print fixture really slices with no shown warning.
- **Timing.** The bounds (`test_mcp_runtime.cpp:142` at 1 s, the 200 ms and 100 ms timeouts, the 5 s waits) on this Mac under build load.
- **The hidden `[history-prefix]` tests** (`test_agent_bridge.cpp:5735, 5741`). They are expected to fail today, so they guard nothing in normal runs.
- **The `MCP bridge` cases.** They hang on this Mac. Their assertions read as sound; the hang was not in scope.
- **Platform-dependent pixel and font checks** on Windows and Linux.

- **#10:** a second preset bundle, loaded the way the loader loads it, now supplies every expected value: the default filament, the offered and set-apart filaments, the plate lists and the "made for" printers. No vendor names are pinned any more.
  - Two of its checks are named preconditions: the MK4's `default_materials` doesn't start with its default, and the H2D excludes at least one plate. A profile update that breaks either fails with a message saying to pick another printer, rather than looking like a loader bug.
  - It also fixes a real bug at `:78`: it compared iterators from two different temporary vectors, which is undefined behaviour.
  - And it fixes the null dereference at `:156`.
- **#12:** I rewrote the test to the current rule (the nozzle-hardness warning, which the chip does list, passes through to the summary unchanged) rather than removing it. No other case covers that.
- **#13:** the guard now reads past blank lines, comments and trailing comments. A define in a form it can't read, a duplicate name, or a string define after the block now fails loudly. A new case also checks that every `warning.msg = X;` in `GCodeProcessor.cpp` uses a constant from the header.
- **`set_resources_dir`:** restored when the test's scratch folder goes away. The Preferences fixture's data dir is now set before its `AppConfig` is built, and restored afterwards.
- **Others:**
  - The send-dialog test now checks the lookup against the table instead of retyping it.
  - The plate-filter and plate-0 guards can now fail (F7).
  - A new locale test checks that `LC_MONETARY` is left as it was, and the false comment is gone.
  - The correlation id is now distinct from the hello's.
  - The nozzle fixture now catches the selected-nozzle leak. The audit's suggested fixture wouldn't have.
  - The theme-file edits find tokens by path, the host-lane times come from the named constants, and the strip width comes from the tool count.
  - The crash at `test_update_check.cpp:147` now fails cleanly, the mojibake is fixed, and three stale test names are corrected.
- **Left alone:**

  - The hard-coded chip padding: making it a token is an app change.

Three things need an app change: the chip's warning filter in `PrintIssueMonitor`, the chip padding token, and how `OrcaHomeBackend` picks the connection action.

**Least sure it compiles:**
- `test_setup_options.cpp`: the new `Profiles` helper keeps a `PresetBundle` as a member and reads several of its fields directly. It relies on `REQUIRE` inside a constructor, and on lambdas inside `CHECK`.

content.text:
I've fixed the audit's findings in four local commits on `claude/assertion-fixes`. Every test suite passes, and so does every harness mode the fixes touch, including a full run of the prompt recorder. Nothing is pushed or merged. The paid live-model tests build but were not run.

The branch sits on `8706ff616a`, the cache-harness session's re-recording of `requests.json`. That session had already removed the six print-issues expectations in `4d663df65c`, so I built on its work rather than duplicating it.

**The commits**
- **a0a7cc1f29, `tests/agent`:** tests no longer keep their own copies of app values. The tool count (28 where the app sends 30) and the 30-name list now come from the tool registry. Model ids come from the provider table, and the MCP client catalogue is compared entry by entry. A check that read the context from before the call it described now reads it after. Temp folders get unique names, so parallel runs can't delete each other's files.
- **960ecb6f88, `tests/jusprin`:**
  - The setup-option tests now take their expected values from the loaded printer profiles, not from today's vendor names.
  - The guard for new OrcaSlicer warning types read only up to the first blank line of the header; it now reads the whole block.
  - The stale "summary counts every warning" test now checks the current rule.
- **6de6197326, shell harness:**
  - In the print-issue readers scenario, a missing issue now fails instead of skipping its checks (253 → 288 checks).
  - One step there never had PETG selected; it now does.
  - The timeline spacing check was already failing on the unchanged branch, because it read the wrong element. It now passes.
- **c6c2394448, prompt suite:**
  - Every conversation in `script.json` now names its plate type, and the recorder selects it only when it differs.
  - A missed skill is now counted as one failure, not two.
  - The live runner exits 2 when there was nothing to compare against, instead of 0.
  - The `answer-from-context` case no longer passes on "pla" inside "plate".

**One thing the fix uncovered.** The plate leaked even within a full run. The recorder goes through `prepare` once per recorded point, and the second and third passes started on the Textured PEI Plate the first pass had selected. So the committed `after-apply` and `after-slice` points recorded a plate that was already PEI and still sliced. I recorded `requests.json` again: those two points now show the plate unsliced after the switch to PEI, and the other 24 points match `8706ff616a`'s recording once timestamps, temp paths, image data and revision numbers are set aside.

**Test results**
| What | Unchanged branch | Fixed branch |
|---|---|---|
| Agent tests (457 cases) | pass | pass, random order, plus the 13 MCP bridge cases |
| `tests/jusprin` (5 binaries) | `jusprin_tests` passes; other four not run | all pass |
| Harness: issue readers | 253 checks pass | 288 pass |
| Harness: timeline | 1 failure | 0 failures |
| Harness: print issues, Check print, setup differences, default | pass | pass |
| Full prompt recording | 12 failures | 0 failures |
| `test_steps.py` | needed the helper | 52 tests pass |

**Left alone**
- **Fragile but correct:** points that expect no skill only because the sample box slices clean, the theme pixel values, and the timing bounds. They fail loudly if they break, and fixing them would mostly be churn.
- **App changes the subagents recommended, not made:**
  - Expose the app's rule for which tools a chat offers, so tests can call it instead of restating it.
  - Export the "no purpose recorded" sentence so tests can reference it.
  - The print-issue monitor's nozzle message says "Filaments 1 are" where OrcaSlicer says "Filaments 1, 1 are".
- **Merge risk:** `d515b36d8d` (journey mode) on the cache-harness branch isn't under this branch, and it also edits `shell_harness.cpp`.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Request bodies as posted (`--request-log`)

`--request-log DIR` (with `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent`,
`--plan-journey` or `--project-prompt-requests`; `DIR` must be new or empty) writes each request
the project chat's Agent posts as `NNNN-request.json`, byte for byte, and
beside it `NNNN-usage.txt`: the project and chat id on the first line, then
each usage object of the response stream. `python3
tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py DIR` prints, for consecutive bodies of
one chat, the first differing byte and its JSON path; `--ignore-cache-control`
drops Anthropic's moving cache breakpoint first. JusPrin writes JSON keys in
sorted order, so on the Responses API `input` comes before `instructions` and
`tools`: a clean append shows up as `$.input[n]`, and a change in
`instructions` or `tools` after it is not reported. Tests: the Catch2
`[request-log]` case and `python3 -m unittest
tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once

def check(directory, ignore_cache_control=False):
    previous, lines = {}, []
    for body_file in sorted(pathlib.Path(directory).glob("[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-request.json")):
        body = body_file.read_bytes()
        if ignore_cache_control:
            body = re.sub(rb'"cache_control":\{[^{}]*\},?', b"", body)
        chat = (body_file.with_name(body_file.name[:4] + "-usage.txt").read_text("utf-8").splitlines() or [""])[0]
        key = (chat, b'"tools":' in body)
        if key in previous:
            name, earlier = previous[key]
            shared = common_prefix(earlier, body)
            where = "identical" if earlier == body else "first difference at byte %d, %s" % (
                shared, first_path(json.loads(earlier), json.loads(body)))
            lines.append("%s %s -> %s: %s" % (chat, name, body_file.name[:4], where))
        previous[key] = (body_file.name[:4], body)
    return lines


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("\n".join(check(sys.argv[1], "--ignore-cache-control" in sys.argv[2:])))

- **Stack:** lldb shows `ProviderAgent::record()` → `next_call()` → `finish_response` → … → `AgentHost::pump_conversation_title()`. So the crash is in the reply to the request that names the chat.

  - When the title reply finishes, `next_call` (around line 549) marks the reply as settled and calls `record()` (line 328).

- **Live app (my guess, untested):** the real app probably throws the same way every time a chat title comes back.
